lines.t: He sits alone at the cracked-screen mirror,
Drowning in a shine that can’t hide the rot inside.
“Who is this stranger in my eyes?
All I ever knew was how to fake it, how to lie.”
A voice cuts straight through his armor,
Pulling every mask off his face.
Questions echo through his history’s hallway,
Down corridors wallpapered with violence and lies,
Raised in a land drunk on sin, pride, and perversion.
A father’s rage like thunder in the night,
A church that painted smiles over chains,
Childhood meals of poison doctrine and dead religion,
In a nation laughing while it burns.
Hands I dodged, still reaching for me,
Blood on my past, but You’re calling me clean.
Sick to the core, I’m done with the scheme,
YahuShua, break me, wake me from this dream.
Mirror don’t lie, I’m a ruined thing,
Heart full of pride, in a land of kings.
I fall on my face, no more in-between,
Kill who I was, let Your mercy intervene.
Now the mirror turns courtroom and mercy seat.
I can’t blame bloodlines, pastors, presidents,
Can’t hide behind culture or trauma anymore.
I see the sickness not just around me but in me—
An empty oil lamp, a hardened heart, a hollow life.“I am that man,” I choke, “a pathetic sinner,
Using fear to control, pride to cover my cracks,
Running from pain, numbing shame,
Mocking Your Name while You kept calling.”
Right there in the glass, I fall like dust.
No more spin, no more justifications,
No more hiding behind a wicked generation.
I own every thought, word, click, and deed,
Let the hammer fall where it belongs—on me.
Hands I dodged, still reaching for me,
Blood on my past, but You’re calling me clean.
Sick to the core, I’m done with the scheme,
YahuShua, break me, wake me from this dream.
Mirror don’t lie, I’m a ruined thing,
Heart full of pride, in a land of kings.
I fall on my face, no more in-between,
Kill who I was, let Your mercy intervene.
You lay my past out like a burning map:
Every night of violence, every secret lust,
Every altar of convenience, every scroll of mockery,
Every Sabbath sold for a paycheck,
Every “Amen” with a dead heart.Then another line appears across it all—
Not the line I crossed, but the line that held me:
A cord that would not snap, a love that would not break,
A patience that waited while I spit in the wind.
The weight crashes down like ten thousand verdicts.
No more “It’s how I was raised,”
No more “That’s just the culture, that’s just the times.”
I see following men was betraying the Truth,
Tradition was my shield against the living God.So I do the one thing I swore I’d never do:
Agree with the Judge against myself.
“I was wrong. You were right.
I deserve the valley and the darkness,
But I’m begging for blood that turns death into life.”
Hands I dodged, still reaching for me,
Blood on my past, but You’re calling me clean.
Sick to the core, I’m done with the scheme,
YahuShua, break me, wake me from this dream.
Mirror don’t lie, I’m a ruined thing,
Heart full of pride, in a land of kings.
I fall on my face, no more in-between,
Kill who I was, let Your mercy intervene.
I stand in the same perverse nation,
Same wicked generation, same polluted air,
But something eternal has shifted inside.
I was born in filth, raised in lies,
Now I live by the Hands that reached for me for years,
And I won’t turn from them again.
